issue.title: Annotated-overwrite archive move renames the open PDF without move notifications; verify what Highlights' presenter follows
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5.5.6.6.6.6.6.6.6.2 note #2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, batch-15 open-pdf-move-coordination phase). The batch-15 lander filed it after checking the source at bob-cli 0a5f0793.

`bob ref create --force` over an annotated reference archives the annotated original before installing the new PDF. The archive step `rename_no_replace(&source, &destination)` at src/native/highlights_ref/overwrite/execute.rs:~1502 renames the open PDF to its archive path inside the outer merging access. Its inverse, `PlatformReverseCoordinator::reverse_file` (overwrite/recovery.rs:~422, rename at ~1624), uses `coordinate_merging_write`. Neither path issues `itemAtURL:willMoveToURL:` or `didMoveToURL:`.

Batch 15 (f00ae66e, 1e923594) added a bounded save-and-move primitive (`coordinate_moving_write`, ForMerging|ForMoving, with move_forward/move_back notifications) for ref rename, but did not apply it here. With Highlights holding the PDF open, it is unknown whether the NSDocument presenter:
(a) follows the archived file object (same inode), so later annotations land in the archive while the fresh PDF sits at the original path;
(b) reloads the new PDF at the original URL; or
(c) shows a conflict dialog.

Either (a) or (c) would be unsaved-annotation risk or confusion of the kind decisions:open-pdf-writes-are-coordinated exists to prevent.

Plan:
1. Reproduce natively with the NSDocument presenter fixture (tests/fixtures/file_coordination/presenter.swift) or real Highlights through scripts/dev/highlights_coordination_acceptance.
2. Decide the intended presenter destination.
3. Either route the archive and reverse moves through the move-coordination scope with explicit move notifications, or record why the merging-only archive is correct.

Not reproduced yet: the Mac was offline during batch 15.

task_type_fields.impact: Possible lost or misplaced Highlights annotations, or a save-conflict dialog, when overwriting an open annotated reference; unverified.
task_type_fields.repro: On macOS with highlights.coordinate_pdf_writes on, open an annotated reference PDF in Highlights (or the presenter.swift NSDocument fixture), run bob ref create --force on it so the annotated original is archived, then check which URL the open document tracks and where later saves land.

issue.creation_reason: Batch-15 phase .2 proposed this follow-up for the lander; the archive transaction predates the epic and was left out of its rename/move coordination scope, so it needs its own native verification.

payload.description: az coordinated rename/move, the id stamp, and create --force publication; this archive move stayed on merging-only access

payload.entry: Resolved by batch-16 phase bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5.5.6.6.6.6.6.6.6.6.3 (bob-cli e557b021) and the lander fix c2b69089. An annotated overwrite now runs inside one bounded coordinate_explicit_pdf_move_with scope (ForMerging|ForMoving) from the live PDF to its preflighted ref_history/...__annotated.pdf. The archive rename is MoveContext::move_forward, which sends willMoveToURL/didMoveToURL. An in-accessor rollback uses move_back through InAccessorMoveReverseCoordinator. Independent crash recovery (PlatformReverseCoordinator) uses a fresh coordinate_moving_write from archive to live, rechecks both hashes inside the accessor, and deletes only a verified owned replacement. Unannotated overwrites stay on a merging write. Never .forReplacing; no uncoordinated fallback. Destination decision, from native NSDocument evidence: the open document follows the archive and later saves land there while the replacement stays byte-identical. After rollback or reverse, later saves land on the restored live PDF and never recreate the archive. The merging-only reverse control showed the unsafe alternative: a later save recreated the archive and left the live path missing. Lander regression fix: e557b021's archive_move_presenter_rollback_inside_move_restores_live_save_target failed deterministically on macOS CI on 29d6105b (run 40470693115) and 017b6927 (run 40479500571). Scratch macOS CI diagnostics (deleted ci/b16-presenter-diag, run 40481907132) showed NSDocument applies move notifications and re-reads about 0.5-0.6 s after the request ends. Because a round trip leaves the URL and text unchanged, the test edited before that re-read and the re-read discarded the edit. The production rollback was correct once settled. c2b69089 adds wait_for_reloaded_document. Verification: scratch run 40484462394 passed all 13 macOS coordination tests three times, and master CI 40485333363 on c2b69089 is green on ubuntu, macOS (both test steps; all five archive_move_presenter cases ok), lint, and package. Limitation: the real-Highlights guided run of scripts/dev/highlights_coordination_acceptance remains unrun (Mac offline); the re-read observation is recorded on bob-cli-ay for that run.
